newsitem.title: USA: Zen-Noh elevator in Louisiana resumes operations.
newsitem.headline: Zen-Noh elevator in Louisiana resumes operations.

text.p: Zen-Noh Grain Corp's loading elevator in Louisiana, which was shut down after an accident in February, resumed operations on June 25, a company official said.
"We are back in business," said Gary Wunsch, vice president and secretary of Zen-Noh Grain Corp. "We are ready to go."
"We have completed loading five grain vessels and one woodchip vessel," Wunsch told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The grain loading facility, located in Convent, La., at mile 162 on the Mississippi River, has an annual handling capacity of 400 million to 500 million bushels of grain, he said.
The elevator was closed February 20 after a vessel collided with the dock and structure of the Zen-Noh terminal.
In early April, the company said the elevator may not resume operations until August at the earliest.
Zen-Noh Grain Corp is a subsidiary of Zen-Noh, or the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations, which is Japan's major importer of U.S. corn.
